hypotheses.justification: The proof uses SFinite μH in only one place: the call `measurable_density H μH`, where it is needed for `Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'`. The other lemmas the proof calls do not take it: HaarQuotient.lintegral_density_mul_eq_one and lintegral_withDensity_eq_of_admissible (which in turn calls map_mk_withDensity_eq_smul_measure). SFinite μH follows from the other hypotheses. (1) H inherits SecondCountableTopology from G through Mathlib's subtype instance. (2) H is closed (hH) in the locally compact G, so Mathlib's `IsClosed.locallyCompactSpace` (Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean) gives `LocallyCompactSpace H`. (3) The instance `sigmaCompactSpace_of_locallyCompact_secondCountable` (Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean) then gives `SigmaCompactSpace H`. (4) μH is a Haar measure, so the instance `IsHaarMeasure.sigmaFinite` (MeasureTheory/Group/Measure.lean, line 921) makes it σ-finite; that instance needs only Group, TopologicalSpace, MeasurableSpace and SigmaCompactSpace. σ-finite implies s-finite. So the fix is to delete the binder and start the proof with `haveI : LocallyCompactSpace H := hH.locallyCompactSpace`; instance search should then supply SFinite μH to measurable_density, and the rest of the proof is unchanged. There is no degenerate case: if H is trivial, it is compact and the argument still applies.
